stages.visible_description_en: The collar of the third leaf is visible; the seedling has a compact form, while the root system and early leaf area continue to develop.
The collar of the fifth leaf is visible; leaf number and expanded leaf area increase, and the stem base and canopy begin to expand noticeably.
The collar of the seventh leaf is visible; the canopy expands rapidly, and stem and internode elongation become more pronounced.
Vegetative growth is vigorous; plant height, leaf area, and internode length increase rapidly.
Upper leaves expand rapidly, and the stem grows taller as the plant gradually develops its pre-tasseling form.
The tassel is fully emerged at the top; the plant approaches its maximum height, and the main canopy and stem structure are largely established.
Silks emerge from the ear husks as the plant enters the pollination period; the vegetative organs remain broadly stable.
Kernels enter the milk and rapid grain-filling stage; ear mass increases, while plant height and the main leaf arrangement remain largely stable.
Kernels reach physiological maturity; the leaves and stems show pronounced senescence, yellowing, or drying.
